covers: The public marketing/content surface: landing page, destinations (index + per-country SEO pages), guides, use-cases, support/FAQ, and the legal (terms/policy) pages. Everything here is publicly indexable except where noted.
note_on_scope: Marketing copy itself (headlines, FAQ text, per-destination prose) is NOT duplicated here verbatim — it already lives in src/content/*.ts as clean typed data and re-reading feedAI would just be a stale copy of it. This topic describes the STRUCTURE: what data feeds what page, how many of each exist, and the actual code-level behavior/gotchas.

landing_page.content_source: src/content/landing.ts — landingContent object: nav items, hero (title/body/popular countries), a curated `destinations` array of 5 countries (USA/Japan/UK/France/Turkey) shown as the homepage grid, 3 `steps`, 3 `benefits`, 4 `faqs`, support links, app store links (Android package com.uplisoft.velocityesim, iOS id6768258284).
landing_page.gotcha: landing.ts's 5-country `destinations` array is a SEPARATE, smaller dataset from seo-pages.ts's 18-country `destinationPages` array (f039) — the homepage grid and the full /destinations directory are not generated from the same source and can drift out of sync (e.g. a new country added to one won't automatically appear in the other).

seo_content_pages.type: SeoContentPage: {kind:'destination'|'guide'|'use-case', slug, path, title, description, heading, eyebrow, intro, sections[], faqs[], relatedLinks[]}
seo_content_pages.counts: 18 destinationPages (usa, europe, japan, turkey, france, uk, germany, italy, spain, greece, portugal, switzerland, thailand, uae, mexico, canada, australia, indonesia), 5 guidePages (what-is-an-esim, esim-vs-roaming, how-to-install-esim, internet-abroad, esim-vs-local-sim), 2 useCasePages (business-travel, remote-work) = 25 total SEO content pages as of 2026-08-19.
seo_content_pages.shared_renderer: ALL 25 pages render through one component, SeoContentPageView (src/app/SeoContentPage.tsx), consumed by src/app/destinations/[slug]/page.tsx, src/app/guides/[slug]/page.tsx, src/app/use-cases/[slug]/page.tsx — same layout for all three content kinds, only the data differs (f042).
seo_content_pages.static_generation: Each [slug] route calls generateStaticParams() returning every slug from its respective array, so all 25 pages are statically generated at build time, not rendered per-request (f043).
seo_content_pages.destinations_index: src/app/destinations/page.tsx: with no ?country= query param, renders a static hero + a card grid of all 18 destinationPages linking to their detail pages. With a ?country= param present, it instead renders DestinationPlans (src/app/destinations/DestinationPlans.tsx, live package search for that country — covered in ui-components-styling.json's data-shaping section) instead of the static grid — same route, two very different render paths gated on a query param.

guides_and_use_cases.note: Same SeoContentPageView pattern as destinations; guides parent breadcrumb is '/' (home) rather than a guides index page — there is no src/app/guides/page.tsx index, only the [slug] detail route. Same for use-cases: no index page, only src/app/use-cases/[slug]/page.tsx.

support_page.content_source: Own hardcoded arrays (supportCategories: 6 categories — Getting started/Installation/Connection issues/Plans & top-ups/Payments & refunds/Account & security; faqs: 10 Q&A items) defined INSIDE this component file, not in src/content/ — a separate dataset from landing.ts's 4 FAQs, with no shared source (f041).
support_page.search: Client-side substring filter (normalizeSearch) over both categories and FAQs simultaneously as the user types; no server round-trip.
support_page.contact: mailto: link to esim@uplisoft.com (SUPPORT_EMAIL constant, shared with legal.ts).

legal_pages.content_source: src/content/legal.ts — termsDocument and policyDocument, both typed as LegalDocument {title, lastUpdated, sections:[{title,paragraphs[]}]}. Terms has 9 sections, Privacy Policy has 11 sections, both dated 'May 9, 2026'.
legal_pages.rendering: src/app/terms/page.tsx and src/app/policy/page.tsx are thin wrappers around one shared LegalDocumentPage component (src/app/LegalDocumentPage.tsx), passing termsDocument/policyDocument respectively.
legal_pages.content_summary_terms: Agreement, the service (third-party operator dependency), eligibility/accounts (18+, OTP), acceptable use, fees & purchases (non-refundable once activated), connectivity disclaimer, IP, limitation of liability, contact.
legal_pages.content_summary_policy: Overview, information collected (account/verification, profile/usage, transaction data, support comms, optional biometrics — kept on-device only), how used, sharing (operators/payment processors/infra, never sold), retention, security, user rights, international transfers, children (under-13 not targeted), changes, contact.

branding.navbar_logo: Navbar.tsx uses public/logo-icon.png (transparent AND colored, cropped from logo-full.png) as of 2026-08-24 (f062) — the earlier public/logo-no-bg.png rendered white-on-white/invisible once content pages went light-themed (f056). SiteFooter.tsx still uses the solid-background public/app-logo.png on its plain white background; the two marks are intentionally different assets, not an inconsistency to 'fix'.
branding.og_image_cache_busting: src/lib/seo.ts's ogImage.url appends a manual ?v=<ogImageVersion> query string (currently '3'). Bump ogImageVersion whenever public/og/esim2you-og.png's bytes change, or link-preview crawlers keep serving a cached copy of the old image since the URL is otherwise static (f063).
